Answer at least **5** of the following questions:

1.  What data did you think you'd find that you weren't able to find?

Before starting this project, I was unsure if I would be able to find the kind of crime data I needed for Washington state counties beyond just general crime statistics. After making a request for data from the Washington Association of Sheriffs and Police Chiefs, I was able to obtain a list of all logged offenses in Washington 2020-2025. Having a list of every single specific offense allowed me to divide the offenses into violent and nonviolent crime. Initially, I just just thinking about crime generally, but having this specific data has allowed me to add a dimension to my project: the impact of law enforcement and social spending on both violent and nonviolent crime rates.

2.  What most surprised you about the data you've been working with?

I was surprised to learn that social services spending is a lot higher than police spending in many areas.

3.  What questions do you still have? What would help you answer them?

I want to compare data across years. I have crime data from 2020-2025 and I could obtain spending data within this range. I have the tools I need to make this comparison, I just need to think about how I will go about it. Using even just one other year makes my questions more interesting because it changes from an exploration of if more spending in one category is associated with less (or more) crime to if a change in spending in one category is associated with a change in crime rates.
